speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with agitation, yellowing of your skin and eyes, and abnormal lab findings; could you tell me how long these symptoms have been progressing and if you have any history of liver disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hepatitis B infection.

The patient's history of high-risk sexual behavior combined with new-onset jaundice, agitation (likely from hepatic encephalopathy or early sepsis), and abnormal labs strongly suggests an acute viral hepatitis, with Hepatitis B being the most probable cause given the transmission risk. Cocaine use can also precipitate hemolysis, but the clinical picture fits acute viral hepatitis best.
